units.passage: If you use an AI tool when completing an assignment, it should be cited like any other reference material. However, you should note that the material generated by AI programs may be inaccurate, incomplete, or otherwise problematic. Beware that use may also stifle your own independent thinking and creativity. Example 2 With the advent of Generative AI tools like ChatGPT, many of us have been fortunate to experience their capabilities firsthand. These tools can serve as incredible assistants, akin to calculators in math classes. Utilizing them effectively involves employing them for idea generation, synthesis, and information gathering to gain a comprehensive understanding of various topics. Nonetheless, it is crucial that we, as users, take charge of guiding, verifying, and refining the ultimate answers generated by these tools. Simply copying and pasting without comprehension is ill-advised. Instead, let's harness these tools as extensions of our knowledge base, enabling us to unlock their true power. If you use an AI tool when completing an assignment, it should be cited like any other reference material (with due consideration for the quality of the reference, which may be poor).
units.why: Example 2 repeats the citation rule in its own wording ("cited like any other reference material"), with a note on reference quality; coded as P24 because each example is its own statement.

units.passage: Faculty, staff, peer educators, and students are responsible for ensuring that GenAI use does not compromise honesty or fairness. They should follow the University of Rochester academic honesty policy for their school. Bias: Faculty staff, peer educators, and students should recognize that all GenAI tools are trained on large, unmoderated datasets. This can lead to biased outputs, which might include incomplete or incorrect information or limited representation of diverse views. Users should remain vigilant and avoid incorporating biases and inaccuracies into their work. Privacy and Security: Those using GenAI should adhere to university principles of respect for intellectual property. Users should not upload to public GenAI platforms confidential and/or proprietary information, including moderate or high-risk data from the University of Rochester. Additionally, they should not share personal or sensitive data, including student information, with public GenAI tools and services. Transparency: Faculty, staff, peer educators, and students should disclose when their work has been created, whole or in part, with a GenAI tool.
units.why: Principle "Transparency": all "should disclose when their work has been created, whole or in part, with a GenAI tool". Disclosure with the work: P24.

units.policy: When AI use is allowed on certain assignments, it must be appropriately acknowledged and cited.
units.why: Where allowed, use 'must be appropriately acknowledged and cited' in the second model; it repeats the disclosure rule in a different statement, coded as its own document-level option (P24).

units.passage: Understand expectations. When using generative AI for writing support, review the requirements of the publisher/reviewer/recipient of the finished product regarding disclosure requirements. Some journals, offices, publishers, or educators may require that generative AI be cited in work, potentially in different ways.
units.policy: When using generative AI for writing support, users review the disclosure requirements of the publisher, reviewer or recipient of the finished product; some may require that generative AI be cited, potentially in different ways.
units.why: Users should "review the requirements of the publisher/reviewer/recipient ... regarding disclosure requirements"; this points to disclosure but does not itself mandate it, so P24 with a fit note.
units.fit_note: Tells users to check the recipient's disclosure rules instead of requiring disclosure itself.

units.passage: impermissible use of generative AI tools (ChatGPT being one of many) in fulfilling curricular requirements will be considered a violation of the Honor Code and adjudicated by the Honor Council. Irresponsible use of generative AI tools includes but is not limited to failure to critically evaluate the accuracy of the generated content (whether text, video, or audio). Impermissible use of generative AI tools includes but is not limited to inappropriate citation of generated content and the use of generated content in violation of course instructions.
units.why: Impermissible use includes "inappropriate citation of generated content", so AI content must be cited appropriately: P24, with a fit note that no citation format is given.
units.fit_note: Frames improper citation as a violation without stating what a proper citation includes.

units.passage: AI technology is to be used in accordance with: (i) academic and student codes of conduct/honor codes; (ii) any ethical and professional standards applicable to a particular course or program; (iii) academic standards pertaining to attribution and citations; (iv) University/Campus policies, procedures, and other guidelines; and (v) applicable laws, rules, or regulations.
units.policy: AI technology is to be used in accordance with academic standards pertaining to attribution and citations.
units.why: Citing 'academic standards pertaining to attribution and citations' as a binding standard for AI use points to attribution duties, but only generally; kept under P24 with a fit note.
units.fit_note: General reference to attribution standards; no disclosure mechanism specified.

units.passage: for writing assignments, use it to assist rather than replace your research and writing processes, and always document and describe your use.
units.why: The same sentence says to 'always document and describe your use': disclosure of AI use with submissions, P24, should.

units.passage: Commit to using GenAI tools with care, making sure you do not copy GenAI output directly into your work without attribution or simply replace your own intentional, purposefully composed work with GenAI
units.why: Students should not 'copy GenAI output directly into your work without attribution': disclosure and attribution of copied AI output, P24.
units.fit_note: Also says not to simply replace one's own composed work with AI output.

units.passage: Quote, paraphrase, and cite GenAI-generated text just like you would quote, paraphrase, and cite any other external source material in your written work.
units.why: Students must 'quote, paraphrase, and cite GenAI-generated text just like' other external source material: disclosure by citation, P24, with AI treated as an outside source.
units.fit_note: Treats AI as an external source under existing citation conventions (P45 idea). | Other coder: Treats AI text like an external source for citation; note tension with P96 (AI not a source) is not stated.

units.passage: When sharing your work in progress with your instructor, a peer reviewer, or a writing consultant, tell them if you’ve used GenAI tools during your composing process.
units.why: Students 'tell them if you've used GenAI tools' when sharing work in progress with instructors, peers or consultants: disclosure with submissions, P24.
units.fit_note: Covers drafts shared with instructors, peer reviewers and writing consultants, not only final submissions.

units.passage: To maintain academic integrity, students must disclose any AI-generated material they use and properly attribute it, including in-text citations, quotations, and references.
units.why: In Open Use, students 'must disclose any AI-generated material they use and properly attribute it': disclose and cite, P24, must.
units.fit_note: Sample statement; also lists in-text citations, quotations and references.

units.passage: To maintain academic integrity, students must disclose any use of AI-generated material.
units.why: In Moderate Use, students 'must disclose any use of AI-generated material' and use attributions: disclose and cite, P24.
units.fit_note: Sample statement; also requires in-text citations, quotations and references.

units.passage: Any use of AI-generated content should be clearly cited.
units.why: "Any use of AI-generated content should be clearly cited." Requires acknowledging AI use in the submission without tool/prompt detail, so P24.

units.passage: However, it must be used responsibly and with appropriate citation.
units.why: 'it must be used responsibly and with appropriate citation' requires citation of permitted AI use, so P24.

units.passage: If this is the case, they should remember to cite the AI.
units.why: "they should remember to cite the AI. Instructors will have information on how they would like classes to cite". Citation required, instructor sets the format, P24.

units.passage: To ensure academic integrity, students must openly disclose any AI-generated material they utilize and provide proper attribution.
units.why: "students must openly disclose any AI-generated material they utilize and provide proper attribution" is a disclosure requirement with each submission, so P24 must. It appears identically in the Open and Moderate statements; coded once.

units.passage: This includes in-text citations, quotations, and references.
units.why: Specifies the form of attribution: 'in-text citations, quotations, and references'. This names the citation format, close to P25, but without tool/prompt details, so partial fit.
units.fit_note: Specifies citation forms (in-text, quotations, references) rather than tool or prompt details.

units.passage: within limited circumstances, and with proper attribution, AI programs may be used as a tool
units.why: Sample (Bryant): AI may be used "within limited circumstances, and with proper attribution"; permitted with attribution, P24.
units.fit_note: Also limits use to limited circumstances. | Also grants limited permission as a tool, which P24 does not capture.

units.passage: should be used with caution and proper citation
units.why: Sample (UNH): if permitted, AI tools "should be used with caution and proper citation"; citation requirement, P24.

units.passage: Any student work submitted using AI tools should clearly indicate what work
units.why: Sample (Colorado): work using AI "should clearly indicate what work is the student's work and what part is generated by the AI"; disclosure, P24.

units.passage: You will be provided with examples of how to cite your use of this tool in your writing.
units.why: Bryant sample: "You will be provided with examples of how to cite your use of this tool"; the instructor supplies citation help, P24 as the nearest type.
units.fit_note: Instructor commitment to supply citation examples rather than a student duty.

units.passage: students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work
units.why: Sample (UMass Amherst): "students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work"; cite AI use, P24.

units.passage: clearly attribute what text was generated by the AI tool
units.why: Sample (UMass Amherst): "I expect you to clearly attribute what text was generated by the AI tool" e.g. a different font colour; marking AI text where used, P24.
units.fit_note: Marks AI-generated text in place, e.g. different colored font or parenthetical. | Marks AI text at the place it appears (P27 is for code), so P24 is nearest.

units.passage: Students should indicate how AI tools informed their process and the final product, including how you validated any AI-generated citations, which may be invented by the AI.
units.why: Iowa sample: "Students should indicate how AI tools informed their process and the final product"; process-level disclosure, P24.

units.passage: properly attributing AI-assisted contributions in research and academic work
units.why: Transparency: "clearly documenting the use of AI-generated content, properly attributing AI-assisted contributions in research and academic work"; disclosure, P24.

units.passage: When using generative AI, users must acknowledge the use of nontrivial AI-generated content and avoid plagiarism.
units.why: "users must acknowledge the use of nontrivial AI-generated content and avoid plagiarism"; disclosure with a triviality threshold, P24.
units.fit_note: Threshold: only nontrivial AI-generated content must be acknowledged.

units.passage: This includes properly citing AI-generated content in academic work and ensuring that AI-generated content does not violate academic integrity policies.
units.why: "properly citing AI-generated content in academic work"; P24.
